note: Narration for the revised NASA demo. Spoken by the Windows built-in text-to-speech voice (synthetic voice, disclosed). Every statement matches a figure shown in the app.

lines.text: Four questions of NASA Earth data: what is changing, where, how much, and is it significant?
lines.caption: What is changing? Where? How much? Is it significant?

lines.text: In one Amazon study box, MERRA-2 shows rainfall falling fast. A second record agrees on direction, at about half the rate.
lines.caption: MERRA-2: −0.541 mm/day per decade · GPCP: −0.282 · same direction, about half the rate

lines.text: The gap opens in 2005, when the rain-gauge input changed.
lines.caption: The records part in 2005: a documented change in the rain-gauge input

lines.text: In northern Alaska, two records agree.
lines.caption: Northern Alaska warming: supported by two independent records

lines.text: Then a what-if hurricane over real Houston refineries: exposure, not a forecast.
lines.caption: Hypothetical hurricane · real refineries (EIA) · exposure, not a forecast
